newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italy's Olivetti H1 revenues drop.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italy's Olivetti H1 revenues drop.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti, battling to return to profitability after years in the red, said on Thursday consolidated revenues for the first half of 1997 dropped 10.4 percent from the same 1996 period.
The loss-making group's revenue stood at 3.1 trillion lire ($1.7 billion), not including sales from mobile phone consortium Omnitel, Olivetti said in a statement.
However, Olivetti said that the drop was smaller than that seen in the second half of 1996, when revenues plunged 20 percent compared with the previous year.
Its total net financing requirement at the end of the first half of 1997 was about 2.5 trillion lire against 2.455 trillion level at the end of June 1996.
"The board stressed the positive trend of the financial situation over the last 12 months," the company said in a statement following a board meeting.
"The great efforts of the management allowed the group, despite the difficulties, to keep the net financing requirement at about the same level as at the end of June 1996," it said.

Rodolfo De Benedetti, son of former Olivetti chairman Carlo De Benedetti, resigned from the board, a move which Olivetti said was consistent with the group's "newly acquired status of public company."
Carlo De Benedetti resigned from his chairmanship last September after he failed to bring the company back to profit. He has since become honorary chairman.
Olivetti, now guided by managing director Roberto Colaninno, has said already it does not expect to turn a profit in 1997, which will make this its seventh consecutive year in the red.

Colaninno has said he expects a recovery in profitibility of information technology interests like computer systems maker Olsy (Olivetti Solutions) and printer maker Lexikon, but these are not expected to offset losses in telecoms interests Telemedia and Omnitel.
Olivetti has a 35.5 percent stake in Omnitel.

The mobile phone consortium said on Wednesday it posted a first half net loss of 172 billion lire against a 259 billion lire loss in the first half of 1996. In the first six months of this year sales rose 178 percent to 680 billion lire.
Omnitel added that it was on track to achieve its aim of breakeven in 1998.
Olivetti's result statement came out after the markets had closed. Olivetti shares finished the day up 29 lire at 675 lire.
